title: Cache Me If You Can: LLM Inference with llm-d (with fun drawings)
tldr: A step-by-step tour of llm-d: how the endpoint picker filters, scores and picks a pod, and where prefix-aware routing, KV offloading and prefill/decode disaggregation fit. Most of the talk is a practical guide to flow control: saturation detectors, fairness policies and priority holdback.

key_points.text: Once one model server fills up, adding replicas needs smarter routing than round robin, or you keep recomputing cache.
The gateway asks llm-d's endpoint picker (EPP) which pod in an InferencePool to use; the key resources are the EPP, InferenceObjective, InferencePool, Gateway and HTTPRoute.
The EPP filters, scores, then picks. It estimates which prefixes each pod holds from the requests it sent; it does not read pod caches.
Prefix affinity can pile traffic onto one hot pod; adding a load score trades cache hits against queue time.
KV offload to CPU keeps long agentic sessions reusable; prefill/decode disaggregation separates bursty prefill from steady decode.
Batch inference runs through an OpenAI-compatible batch gateway and an async processor that dispatches when there is room.
Flow control: priority bands hold per-tenant queues, and it only gates when the pool is saturated. Fairness policies include global strict (oldest first), round robin, and least-served first.
Saturation detectors can count requests or tokens, read engine utilization (which lags), or combine both; gate too early and you lose throughput, too late and GPUs oversaturate.
Priority holdback stops batch from being admitted above a pool saturation threshold, so real-time latency stays as if batch were not there.
Other levers: SLO-based ordering, headroom, quota-based priority, and evicting batch work back to the queue for retry.
Tune by symptom, one knob at a time, and check llm-d's prefix guesses against vLLM's own metrics.

numbers.text: Priority holdback example: batch held back when total pool saturation is above 0.6, tested on H100.

open_gaps.text: Output-token estimation is off by default and needs extra infrastructure; request-count detectors break down when request sizes vary widely.
Utilization-based detection lags and can over-admit.
There are many knobs and little tooling to see their effect; the speaker built a replay visualizer and interactive explainer and hopes to contribute them.

opportunities.text: Mix batch and real-time traffic on one pool, turn on priority holdback, and measure real-time P95.
